title: Cohomology classes of augmented computing resolution f-maps
statement: Let $f:X'\to X$ be a scheme morphism [def-pc-scheme], let $F,F'$ be module sheaves on $X,X'$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and let $D,E$ be their computing resolutions [def-sc-module-cup-resolution-data]. Let $\varphi:F\to f_*F'$ be a coefficient f-map [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap]. Let $u:D.K\to f_*E.K$ be a sheaf cochain map, pushforward applied termwise, such that $u^0a_D^0=f_*(a_E^0)\varphi$. Define $\Gamma_f(u)$ by global sections followed by restriction along $f^{-1}(X)=X'$. For each degree $n$ and global kernel cycles $a,a'$ with underlying sections satisfying $a'=\Gamma_f(u)^n(a)$, one has $E.\mathrm{class}_n(a')=\varphi^*(D.\mathrm{class}_n(a))$. The coefficient f-map and computing resolutions are arbitrary. No tensor pairing is assumed.

source.place: cohomology-lemma-functoriality-cech, injective resolution comparison diagram; Remark 01FB

proof.text: Define the sections isomorphism degreewise by presheaf.mapIso along inverse-image(top)=top. Naturality of the differentials makes it a cochain isomorphism. Define the additive global map by taking sections of u and composing with the inverse sections isomorphism.

Use the system C already selected by moduleCohomologyFMap. Lift the identities from D.I to C.J and from E.I to C.I with InjectiveResolution.desc. Composing with D.comparison and E.comparison gives maps from the computing resolutions to these fixed injective resolutions. The resolutionSectionsIso naturality identity follows from isoRightDerivedObj_hom_naturality and mapHomologyIso_inv_naturality.

The two maps D.K to C.K, obtained via D.comparison, the identity lift and C.beta, or via u, the pushforward of E.comparison and the identity lift, and C.lambda, agree on the augmentation by hu, D.over, E.over and C.compatible. Construct their homotopy explicitly: descend the degree-zero difference across the exact augmentation short complex by injectivity; at the next degree subtract the previous homotopy term and descend by exactness and injectivity again. Inductively the cochain equations and d composed with d equal to zero give the necessary vanishing. Apply global sections and homology to get equality of the two homology composites.

The sections isomorphisms commute with the comparison from E.K to C.I by presheaf naturality; C.sections identifies C.a with the canonical sections isomorphism. Combine this with the homotopy equality and naturality of the injective-resolution identifications. Cancel the invertible replacement homology map to obtain the equality of maps on additive global homology. Naturality of the cycles map and homology projection identifies the image of the source cycle with the specified target cycle, across scalar rings. Naturality of mapHomologyIso identifies the resulting formulas with D.class and E.class, giving the asserted equation.

theorem cupResolution_class_fmap {X X' : Scheme.{v}} (f : X' ⟶ X)
    {F : X.Modules} {F' : X'.Modules}
    (D : CupAcyclicResolution F) (E : CupAcyclicResolution F')
    (φ : F ⟶ (pushforward f).obj F')
    (u : D.K ⟶ ((pushforward f).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj E.K)
    (hu : D.augmentation.f 0 ≫ u.f 0 =
      φ ≫ (pushforward f).map (E.augmentation.f 0))
    (n : ℕ)
    (a : ((((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace).mapHomologicalComplex
      (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj D.K).sc n).moduleCatLeftHomologyData.K)
    (a' : ((((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X'.toRingedSpace).mapHomologicalComplex
      (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj E.K).sc n).moduleCatLeftHomologyData.K)
    (ha : a'.val = (cupResolutionGlobalMap f u).f n a.val) :
    E.class n a' = moduleCohomologyFMap f φ n (D.class n a)
